sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. Petitioner, in this writ petition, seeks to assail the action of the Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC) in taking coercive measure for eviction of their shops situated at Bhimatangi Chhak, Ward Nos.60 and 61, Bhimatangi Housing Board, Bhubaneswar in the district of Khordha of the Petitioners.
3. It is submitted by Mr. Das, learned counsel for the Petitioners that the Petitioners are running their shops covering Ward Nos. 60 and 61 of Bhimatangi Chhak.

Although they are street vendors as per the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 (for short, 'the Act') no survey has yet been made by the BMC authority in consonance with Sections 3 and 18 of the Act.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further, they are identified and issued with certificate-cum-letter of recommendation and registration certificate by the Health and Family Welfare Department Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Certificate of Registration under FSS Act, 2006 and they have been issued with ID cards from time to time valid up to 6th February, 2023.

entities.text: Health and Family Welfare Department Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However, in spite of all these, BMC authorities // 2 // are threatening to evict and demolish the shop of the Petitioner without issuing any notice to the Petitioners.
It is submitted that law is well-settled that even a trespasser cannot be evicted without following due procedure of law.

Finding no other alternative,
the Petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

5. Mr. Dash, learned Counsel for the BMC submits that since the Petitioners allege coercive action by the BMC, they may approach the appropriate authority of the BMC for redressal of their grievances.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the unusual situation of resurgence of COVID-19, this Court, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case of the Petitioner, disposes of the writ petition with a direction that in the event the Petitioners submit representation(s) to the Commissioner, BMC (OP No.3) along with relevant documents and information within a period of two weeks hence along with certified copy of this order, he shall do well to consider and pass a reasoned order thereon in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of four weeks therefrom and intimate the same to the Petitioner.

6.1 Till disposal of the representation(s), if filed within the period stipulated hereinabove, no coercive action shall be taken for eviction of the shops of the Petitioners situated in Ward Nos.60 and 61 of Bhimatangi Chhak and Bhimatangi Housing Board, Bhubaneswar if not already evicted in the meantime.
Issue urgent certified copy of the order on proper application.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Although they are street vendors as per the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 (for short, 'the Act') no survey has yet been made by the BMC authority in consonance with Sections 3 and 18 of the Act.
Further, they are identified and issued with certificate-cum-letter of recommendation and registration certificate by the Health and Family Welfare Department Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Certificate of Registration under FSS Act, 2006 and they have been issued with ID cards from time to time valid up to 6th February, 2023.
It is submitted that law is well-settled that even a trespasser cannot be evicted without following due procedure of law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Taking into consideration the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the unusual situation of resurgence of COVID-19, this Court, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case of the Petitioner, disposes of the writ petition with a direction that in the event the Petitioners submit representation(s) to the Commissioner, BMC (OP No.3) along with relevant documents and information within a period of two weeks hence along with certified copy of this order, he shall do well to consider and pass a reasoned order thereon in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of four weeks therefrom and intimate the same to the Petitioner.
6.1 Till disposal of the representation(s), if filed within the period stipulated hereinabove, no coercive action shall be taken for eviction of the shops of the Petitioners situated in Ward Nos.60 and 61 of Bhimatangi Chhak and Bhimatangi Housing Board, Bhubaneswar if not already evicted in the meantime.
